newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Moslem official says U.S. wants him ousted.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Moslem official says U.S. wants him ousted.

text.p: A top Moslem official said on Tuesday that the United States had been putting pressure on the Bosnian government to remove him because he allegedly posed an obstacle to a U.S. military aid programme.
"It is true, there are certain pressures...When we are talking about such behaviour, I think it is neither democratic nor usual," Hasan Cengic, the Bosnian deputy defence minister told reporters.
Western media have portrayed Cengic as hostile to Washington's arms programme, which required the Bosnian government to remove Islamic foreign fighters and sever military ties with Iran.
The Washington Post sparked a flurry of speculation in Sarajevo when it published a story saying U.S. officials were pushing for Cengic's removal.
American officials believed Cengic was blocking the programme, aimed at strengthening the Moslem-Croat army against militarily superior Serb forces, the paper reported.

The newspaper reported in detail about Cengic's alleged connections with Iran, describing him as a key figure in supplying the Moslem-led Bosnian government with weapons during four years of a U.N. arms embargo.
Iran and other Islamic countries shipped arms to Bosnia at a time when the Moslem-led army was badly outgunned by Serb forces.

The United States delayed a "train and equip" programme for Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation military until it was satisfied Sarajevo authorities had removed Islamic foreign fighters from the country, severed military ties to Iran and begun merging Croat and Moslem armies.
"The pressure had been applied through September," Cengic said.
He insisted that there was no official discussion about the matter in the Bosnian government.
"We are a sovereign country and we shall conduct our own policy, both a general (policy) and personnel (policy)," Cengic said.
